notes.note: No screen: COACCT01 sends and receives no map. It issues EXEC CICS RETRIEVE INTO(MQTM) and takes the request queue name from MQTM-QNAME, so the program expects to be started with an MQ trigger message; the trigger monitor, process and initiation queue that would start CDRA are not in the scanned inputs, so how CDRA is entered stays open.

Queue names: the request queue is a run-time value (MQTM-QNAME) and is not derived here; the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT and the error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR are literals. The module README defines CARDDEMO.REQUEST.QUEUE and CARDDEMO.RESPONSE.QUEUE instead, which the program does not name - which definitions are installed is a question for the MQ administrator.

Not pseudo-conversational: one task drains the queue (MQGET under syncpoint with a 5000 ms wait, EXEC CICS SYNCPOINT per message) and ends with a plain EXEC CICS RETURN when MQGET reports no message available. ACCTDAT is read only (EXEC CICS READ, no UPDATE).

No screen: CODATE01 sends and receives no map. It issues EXEC CICS RETRIEVE INTO(MQTM) and takes the request queue name from MQTM-QNAME, so the program expects to be started with an MQ trigger message; the trigger monitor, process and initiation queue that would start CDRD are not in the scanned inputs, so how CDRD is entered stays open.

Queue names: the request queue is a run-time value (MQTM-QNAME) and is not derived here; the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE and the error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR are literals. The module README defines CARDDEMO.REQUEST.QUEUE and CARDDEMO.RESPONSE.QUEUE instead, which the program does not name.

Not pseudo-conversational and touches no file: per message it runs ASKTIME/FORMATTIME, puts the date and time on the reply queue, syncpoints, and ends with a plain EXEC CICS RETURN when MQGET reports no message available.
